methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Pre-Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $3M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Durin is a pre-seed-stage infrastructure and logistics company founded by Ted Feldmann that has raised $3.4M to date. The comparable universe consists of one identified private peer (Watoga Technologies) and no public comparables, limiting the breadth of benchmarking available.

The stage-progression method is the applicable valuation approach given data constraints. Using total capital raised of $3.4M as a baseline proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for pre-seed to seed-stage advancement, this method yields an implied valuation of $8.5M. This represents a modest markup from deployed capital, consistent with early-stage risk profiles in infrastructure logistics.

The triangulated valuation range stands at $7M to $10M, with a median of $8M supported by the stage-progression framework. Key uncertainties include the sparsity of the comparable set—reliance on a single private peer and absence of public market benchmarks limits conviction in the multiplier applied. Additionally, stage-progression methodology alone cannot account for company-specific unit economics, market traction, or competitive positioning relative to Watoga Technologies. A more robust analysis would require additional private comparable data or visibility into revenue/growth metrics to cross-check the implied valuation range.
